name: ELEGANT
summary: The ELEGANT programme used underground scintillation detectors for rare-event searches. The ELEGANT-VI calcium-fluoride configuration specifically searched for calcium-48 neutrinoless double-beta decay and preceded CANDLES.
detection_principle: CaF2(Eu) scintillators act as source and detector. Surrounding scintillators veto external radiation, while energy and pulse-shape selections reduce radioactive backgrounds near the high 48Ca decay endpoint.

results.summary: The ELEGANT-VI search set a 48Ca half-life limit using calcium-fluoride scintillators.

science_scope: A neutrinoless double-beta-decay signal would establish lepton-number violation. Converting a half-life constraint into an effective Majorana mass requires a decay mechanism and nuclear matrix elements; a null search is not a neutrino-mass measurement.
